doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Buddy Rich tour, Lester Young and Ben Webster on 52nd Street
summary: Why he left New York, two and a half years with Buddy Rich on a State Department tour, plus memories of Lester Young and hearing Ben Webster at 17.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh yeah, okay. What prompted the move to the west coast?
I think mostly there seemed to be maybe like a little slump in what was happening. Of course you know before that, before I went to the west coast I was with Buddy Rich, with the small group.
Oh yeah, I wanted to ask you about that.
For about two and a half years, we had Mike Mainieri and a few other people and Buddy. And that went very well. We just traveled around the world because he had a State © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Department tour, we went to India and South America and Afghanistan and Vietnam, Nepal, just a lot of crazy places. And he had two records too, but they are kind of collector’s items on different labels. But by the way, just to backtrack, I was at Manhattan School of Music for a while, and that’s when I got the offer to go with Buddy. I think I went down to Birdland and someone said he’s looking for somebody, Seldon Powell was leaving. And I think it was my friend again, Arnold Rosen, he said, “Why don’t you get up there and play?” Anyhow I sat in with Buddy and he says, “You got the gig.” Another time I remember going to Birdland and my friend also said, “Why don’t you get up there and play with Lester Young?” So I got up to play and Lester Young tapped me on the back and said, “Go ahead, kid, blow.” So that was nice of him. I remember another thing was Lester Young was walking across the street in New York and this is the famous Lester Young, he’s walking across the street to the White Rose Bar and I’m crossing the street with him. And I said, “Tell me, could you tell me what you think about when you improvise?” So he said, “I just play from here.” That was his answer. You know, just little things that you remember. And the other thing, I’m just going around to different things, just whatever comes to mind that I wanted to tell you. The other thing is when I was about 17, you know I was living in New York, so I went down to 52nd Street and they had all these great players there, Art Tatum, Bird, Erroll Garner. I walked into this, I was able to get in, maybe I looked a little older at the time or whatever, went in with somebody, but who was playing but Ben Webster was playing, and it was beautiful, smoky, and he was sounding so great, and I said that’s what I want to do. So that’s how that started, when I was about 17 I said wow, to be able to play the tenor that way. So that was a big influence.
